You are fixing an injected bug in the Python 'dateutil' repository checked out at /dateutil (do NOT look at any other installed copy of dateutil, no internet). Work only in /dateutil. Rules: never edit or delete files under /dateutil/dateutil/test/ (pre-existing tests must stay untouched); do not add new features; make minimal source edits only.

TASK: There is a deliberately injected bug in /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py. The hidden test that must pass is `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::testFuzzyWithTokens` (that test is NOT in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: fuzzy parsing with the `fuzzy_with_tokens=True` option must return a tuple `(datetime, tokens)` where `tokens` is a list of the non-date string tokens found in the input, e.g. `parser.parse('Today is 25 of September of 2003, exactly at 10:49:41 with timezone -03:00.', fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` returns the datetime plus a token list containing the leftover text tokens; and `parser.parse('I have a meeting on 25 September 2003 at 10:00', fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` etc.).

Investigate the `_parse` method of `parser.parser` (the `fuzzy_with_tokens` code path, the `_parse` signature, `_build_naive`, `_build_tzaware`, and the `parse`/`parser()` entry points) for the injected mutation and fix it minimally so that fuzzy_with_tokens returns the correct (datetime, token-list) pair. Note the token list must be a list of strings (the parts of the input that were not consumed as date/time information).

METHOD: first run the full suite `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` and record the baseline (currently 1064 passed, 43 skipped). Then find the mutation by careful reading of the code (the docstrings in parser.py describe the expected behaviour), fix it, and re-run the full suite. NO pre-existing test may fail after your change. Write throwaway verification scripts in /tmp (never inside /dateutil).

REPORT BACK: the exact file+line+old code+new code of your fix, verification commands and output, and the full-suite result. If you cannot fix it, say so explicitly.

TASK: Two bugs in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py. Both are deliberately injected mutations of the upstream code (small edits that changed behaviour).

BUG 1: `rrule(..., count=0)` must produce an EMPTY recurrence set. Currently `list(rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=datetime(2000,1,1)))` returns millions of dates (it runs to year 9999). The hidden test that must pass is `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testCountZero` (the test itself is NOT in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: count=0 yields no occurrences, and `rrule(DAILY, count=0).count()` should be 0). Find the injected mutation (look at `_iter`, `__init__`, `count()`, `__str__`, `replace()` in rrule.py) and fix it minimally so count=0 behaves as an empty set. Consider also that `str()` of such a rule and `count()` should be sane.

BUG 2: `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testStrAppendRRULEToken` must pass (test not in repo; name describes expected behaviour: the string produced by `str(rrule(...))` / `rrulestr` round-tripping must append the RRULE token correctly, e.g. `str(rrulestr('DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3'))` must contain a line starting with 'RRULE:' and re-parsing that string must give an equivalent rule). Investigate `rrule.__str__`, `_rrulestr._parse_rfc`, `_parse_rfc_rrule` and `rruleset.__str__` for the injected mutation and fix it minimally. Make sure `str()` output can be fed back into `rrulestr()`.

METHOD: first run the full suite `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test -q` and record the baseline (currently 1064 passed, 43 skipped). Then find each mutation by careful reading of the code (compare against how the rest of the code/docstrings say it should behave), fix it, and re-run the full suite. NO pre-existing test may fail after your change. Write your own throwaway verification scripts in /tmp (never inside /dateutil).

REPORT BACK: for each bug: the exact file+line+old code+new code of your fix, the verification commands and their output, and the full-suite result. If you cannot fix one, say so explicitly and leave the file as you found it for that bug.
